note: Independent source rejudgment against committed HEAD 7565a5b4b7ecc7e90254e3a04a00e58871b884c2 after the checkRFC2545NextHops adapter landed in 71b1f3d799. RFC 2545 Section 3: "The value of the Length of Next Hop Network Address field on a MP_REACH_NLRI attribute shall be set to 16, when only a global address is present, or 32 if a link-local address is also included in the Next Hop field." Both branches are directly asserted: the default-originate and SendAnnounce controls compare the exact MP_REACH global-plus-link-local bytes including length 0x20; the Session positive/negative guard pair requires the valid two-address form and no output for an invalid second address. The grouped static-route test independently compares literal sixteen-octet next-hop fields, complete route/EOR framing and successful ownership. The SR Policy config and public encoder tests compare length, literal IPv6 address, reserved octet and NLRI independently under either policy AFI; their native IPv4 cases are separately identified controls under RFC 9830, not RFC 2545 IPv6-width claims. TestFamilyNextHopOriginationAdmission and the API batch, queued-drain, named-commit and post-policy tests require the literal sixteen-octet field for valid global controls, refuse native IPv4 substitution under IPv6 multicast/labeled/unicast roles, and check actual delivered bytes/accounting so a dropped valid control cannot pass. TestFamilyNextHopForwardAdmission and TestRFC2545EffectivePairPolicyAndMixedSibling inspect cached and route-server output after export policy: illegal 4/24/48-byte or empty/eight-byte plain fields are not announced, later valid repairs produce the exact legal sixteen- or thirty-two-octet field, and independently valid legacy sibling NLRI remain. Those inputs isolate effective field width from obsolete pre-policy width. The producing code supports these assertions: MPReachNLRI.nextHopLen derives its count from the same address octets writeNextHops serializes, WriteTo writes that count at the length octet, writeAnnounceUpdate selects 16 or 32 from the admitted optional second address, buildMPReachPlugin writes len(nhBytes), and the effective policy writer and Session boundary validate the family-specific width before advertisement. The ExaBGP encoding fixture compares literal 0x20 pair bytes, and adj-rib-in replay compares the complete live and replay frames with the same 32-byte next-hop field under separately sequenced receiver expectations. test/encode/new-v6.ci contains an exact 0x10 global-only frame assertion; its inherited unproven discrimination status is not changed or claimed newly proven by this source review. The changed checkRFC2545NextHops retains its two different prefixes and global next hops on one IPv6 session, requires FRR to decode exactly the expected global/link-local pair for the on-link route and global alone for the off-link route, and keeps both session checks. FRR 10.7.1 route_vty_out_detail emits the link-local next-hop entry only for BGP_ATTR_NHLEN_IPV6_GLOBAL_AND_LL, so these scope/address assertions discriminate the received 32-byte form from the single-global form; exact wire tests separately pin the length octets directly. Assertion 5 now additionally requires the exact selected, installed BGP prefix and matching active FIB link-local in one native zebra entry through requireRouteInstalledVia, strengthening installation evidence without removing a length assertion. Verdict remains enforced for the length requirement. This note makes no new runtime, mutant or revert observation and does not replace the native discrimination status of any carrier.
